quests.title: Building Something Permanent
quests.description:
You're the one off the last boat. Good - I've a job and no one to give it to.

Rask'jin. Quartermaster, which out here means I'm the one who has to turn a landing spot into a camp before the season turns.

A camp wants a palisade. A palisade wants posts. And sand does not hold a post, mon - I've driven forty of them and watched every one lean over by morning like it was tired.

Reef coral holds. The deep-red kind, that grows out where the current's strongest - not the pretty stuff in the shallows, that crumbles in your hand.

I can't dive for it. But the coconut crabs along the beaches drag it up the sand to line their burrows, so the quick way to get coral is to get it back off a crab.

They're the size of a kodo's head and they have opinions.
quests.accept_text: The crabs on the beaches are hoarding it. They'll fight you for it. They'll lose.
quests.turn_in_text:
This is good stock! Palisade goes up by week's end.

You didn't have to help build something that isn't your home. That you did anyway - I notice that.

quests.title: Eyes on the Cultists
quests.description:
Vessa. I watch the tree line, which is a quiet posting right up until it isn't.

For a week now the smoke over the troll island has been the wrong colour. Not cook-fire smoke. Not green-wood smoke either. Something else is going on that fire and I don't like what the wind brings off it.

Here's the ground. The east bridge off the Landing takes you to Kang'ari's village, and past that the north trail runs on to the old Darkspear camps - Zalazane's now.

I want eyes on the north camp before anybody commits to a fight over it.

Don't engage. I'll say that twice if I have to. Look, remember, come back.

We do this one smart, not angry. Angry comes later and it'll be better for having waited.

objectives.label: the cultist camp north of Kang'ari's village

quests.accept_text: East bridge, past Kang'ari's village, then north to the camp. Don't engage.
quests.turn_in_text: Dat many? ... Good. Now we know what we're walkin' into. Most people who die out dere die because dey walked in blind. Next job's closer to home, and louder.

quests.title: Wings Over the Tree Line
quests.description:
Second job, and this one's close to home and considerably louder.

My signal fires keep going out. That's not weather and it's not the wood - it's the birds.

Isle screechers. Green-and-red jungle things with a voice like a knife on a whetstone, and they nest in the canopy directly above my watch-post. They mob anything that moves, and a lit fire moves plenty.

And a raptor or two has worked out that where the birds are shouting, something is worth coming to look at. So now I've got birds overhead and teeth underneath.

Thin them. Birds and the raptors trailing them both.

I have been shouting over that canopy for nine days and I would like to hear the wind again.
quests.accept_text: They nest in the canopy all round the Landing, and the raptors trail them like dogs.
quests.turn_in_text: Quiet. Actually quiet. I forgot what dat sounded like. Take one of dese - I made dem for myself.

quests.title: Nets Full of Teeth
quests.description:
Tarna. Don't mind the nets, they're all torn anyway.

The Tidal Flats used to be the best fishing on this archipelago. South-east of the Landing - the cays where the tide pulls back and leaves you a mile of wet sand and everything the sea didn't want.

I fished it for eleven years. Every net came back full and my ankles came back fine.

Now every net comes back shredded and my ankles come back stung, and I am getting too old to be surprised by the same thing twice a week.

Flatfin stingers have moved into the silt - they hide under it, so you'll find them with your foot before your eye. Burrowing crabs behind them.

They are not interested in sharing and I've stopped asking.

Stingers first. Then the burrowers. And watch your feet, you hear?
quests.accept_text: South from the Landing till the sand goes grey and the water's at your shins.
quests.turn_in_text: Dat's two good tides of fishing I got back. Not safe yet - da big one's still out dere - but you've earned a pick off my best work.

quests.title: The Shell That Ate the Skiff
quests.description:
Now the part I've not said out loud to anyone at the Landing.

I lost a skiff last month. I've been letting people think it was the tide, because the alternative makes me sound like a woman who's been in the sun too long.

It was not the tide.

Something lives under those cays the size of a hut. A crab, mon - grown fat over forty years on everything the flats leave behind. Shellcrusher, the old fishers called him. Kragg.

He takes the whole boat when he's hungry and lets the fisherman swim, and I have thought about what that means about him more than I'd like.

He comes up when the smaller crabs trailing him go quiet. So kill his courtiers and he'll come looking.

And don't try to out-wait him. He's more patient than you are. Hit him from the side.

I want a trophy. And I want my skiff's anchor back.
quests.accept_text: Under the cays on the Tidal Flats. Kill the crabs trailing him and he'll come.
quests.turn_in_text: Ha! Forty years of crab, and he went down like a bad knot. My anchor?! Oh, you found it. Take whatever you like off his shell, I got what I wanted.

quests.title: Good Cord Is Hard to Find
quests.description:
Talra. Sit if you want, I'll not stop working while we talk.

Hemp rots. Sinew snaps. The sea does not care about either and will prove it to you on the one night you need a net to hold.

The only cord that has ever outlasted a Darkspear storm is cured eel-hide. That's not preference, that's forty years of mending.

The best eels on this archipelago are the bilge eels of Wreck Shallows - the knee-deep flats away up in the far north-east, between the troll island and the dead ships of the Lost Fleet.

I'd go. My hands ache in the cold water now and a net mended badly is worse than a net not mended, so I don't let myself.

I'm out. Properly out, not nearly out.

The wreck crabs will pester you and the eels will shock you. Bring me good lengths - I'll know if you've cheated.
quests.accept_text: East bridge, through the village, past the north camp, then wade north-east till the water's at your knees.
quests.turn_in_text:
Oh, that's lovely. Smooth as silk and mean as a snake.

I'll mend every net on the Landing with this. And I'll make you something out of what's left over.

quests.title: Voices in the Drowned Stone
quests.description:
Come closer. You don't have to be quiet, the spirits aren't listening to us.

Vashj. I speak for the dead of this island, which has been a busy posting lately.

They've been restless a month. Every night, from the north-west, the same thing: low, rhythmic, and - this is the part that's kept me up - not unfriendly.

That's a voice standing guard over something old. I've heard hostile spirits. This isn't that.

The Naga Ruins, on the north-west island. Over the west bridge to the Grotto isle, up its north trail, then across the Sunken Steps ford.

I'm not asking you to fight anything.

I'm asking you to stand in the old stones and hear what I hear, so that there are two of us who have heard it. One person hearing a voice at night is a story. Two is a fact.

Don't talk. Don't take anything. Just listen.

objectives.label: the drowned stones at the Sunken Steps

quests.accept_text: West bridge to the Grotto isle, north trail, wade the Sunken Steps. Stand in the stones and listen.
quests.turn_in_text:
So they spoke to you too. Not in words. In order.

They're guarding something - and they are afraid of whatever comes after them.

Let me think on this. Come back when you're ready for the next part.

quests.title: What the Tide Remembers
quests.description:
I can read the old runes. What I cannot do is read them off the air.

The naga wear them. Tide-etched scales, each one marked with a spiral that is half writing and half weather - and I mean that precisely, because the spiral changes with the water and the writing does not, and I have spent some years failing to explain that to anyone.

The coastguards carry them. So do the tidecallers.

Take them off the ones who've no further use for them.

Bring me enough that I can lay them side by side, because a single scale is a mark and a row of them is a sentence. That's the whole of why I'm asking for more than one.

And please - wash your hands afterwards. Whatever they cure the scales in does not come off a palm by itself.
quests.accept_text: Off the coastguards and tidecallers at the Naga Ruins.
quests.turn_in_text:
... it is a seal.

They are not guarding the temple. They're guarding the door UNDER the temple, and there's a key-keeper standing over it.

That's the name, mon. Warden Ssaleth. End him and the door stays shut.

quests.title: The Warden's Oath
quests.description:
Warden Ssaleth keeps those ruins the way a lock keeps a door. Not out of hatred. Out of oath.

I want that understood before you go, because it changes nothing about what has to happen and I'd still rather you knew.

I can feel the oath on him from here. I can also feel that it's fraying, and an oath that frays does not come apart tidily - it comes apart all at once, on a night nobody chose.

If he falls, that door stays shut a while longer.

If he's left alone, the oath gives out on its own and whatever walks up to the door next will have worse manners and no oath at all.

Thin the guard, find him. He stands where the stones are highest.

His trident cuts, and when you hold still he pulls the strength out of you. So don't hold still, and don't fight him standing in the water.
quests.accept_text: Back to the Naga Ruins. He stands where the stones are highest.
quests.turn_in_text:
The stones are silent. Not gone - silent. I've not heard that in years.

You've bought this island a season at least. This is from the Landing, not from me.

quests.title: The Isle Bites Back
quests.description:
[The elder looks up without surprise.]

Kang'ari. You'll be the one the Landing keeps sending out. Sit.

I'll not waste words on the beasts. Raptors, panthers, serpents, screechers, crabs the size of a cooking pot - all of it thick through the interior now, and thicker every month.

That's not the island turning on us. That's Zalazane's fires in the north pushing everything south onto one trail, and the trail between the Landing and this village is the one they've all ended up on.

So before we talk about what's actually wrong with this place - and we will, and you'll wish we hadn't - the road needs clearing.

Any mix of them. I don't care which. There's nothing personal in this one.

Come back when a person can walk it.
quests.accept_text: The interior's thick with all of them. Any mix. Come back when the road's walkable.
quests.turn_in_text: Good. Da trail's quieter now. Not safe - dis island hasn't been safe in longer than you'd guess - but quieter. Now. About what's really wrong with dis place.

quests.title: The Camps Answer For It
quests.description:
Now the part I've been carrying.

The hostile camps sit north and south of this village, on the isle's two trails. Voodoo trolls, hex trolls, berserkers, headhunters, the fetish-carvers who tend the fires.

All of them Darkspear. All of them ours.

Every one of them was somebody's kin inside the last three years. I knew names. I knew which of them was bad at fishing and which one owed me a canoe.

They are not coming back from what he did to them. I have looked for the road back and there isn't one, and I looked for longer than was good for me.

So I'm asking you to go and finish it, and I'm not going to dress it up as anything cleaner than that.

Start where Vessa's report put them. North trail and south.

I don't ask you to feel good about this fight. I ask you to finish it.
quests.accept_text: North trail and south, at the hostile camps. Start where Vessa's report said.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's done. I felt every one of those.

The camps are quiet. Zalazane still holds the Hollow in the south-east, and the temple under the west isle is still drowned.

But first I need something of yours.

quests.title: What Zalazane Took
quests.description:
Before the last push, something recovered rather than destroyed.

Hexed Darkspear totems. Our own work, twisted by his magic - but not past recognising, and that distinction is the only thing I've had to hold on to for three years.

The voodoo trolls carry them. So do the hex trolls, and so do the carvers at the camp fires.

Bring them here.

I want to study what was done. Not to undo it - I'm old enough to say plainly that I can't. But a thing you understand is a thing somebody after me might undo, and I'd like to leave that person something better than a rumour.

And don't handle the magic still sitting on them if you can help it. I've seen what that kind of hex does to someone who's careless with it, and the carelessness is always small and the result never is.
quests.accept_text: Off the voodoo trolls, the hex trolls and the carvers at the camp fires.
quests.turn_in_text:
This tells me more than I expected. The hex isn't as permanent as I feared.

There may be a way back for some of them. Someday. Not today.

Keep that wherever you keep hope.

quests.title: The Drowned Temple
quests.description:
The Sunken Temple Grotto. West island, cave mouth at the end of the Grotto trail past the west bridge.

It floods with the tide and empties with it, and it has done that since before the Darkspear came to these isles. We held that ground sacred and we held it carefully.

Something ancient has claimed the drowned chambers. Tidelord Gharesh.

I don't know whether Zalazane summoned it or simply failed to stop it, and I have gone back and forth on which answer frightens me more.

Here's the fight, and it's the whole fight: Gharesh moves with the tide. Strong when the water's high. Slower when it's low.

Time it right and that's a thing you can kill. Time it wrong and you are fighting a flood that hits back.

Go at low water, mon. I'll not be more plain than that.
quests.accept_text: Temple door at the end of the west trail, past the bridge. Go at low water.
quests.turn_in_text:
The temple's quiet. Whatever that thing was standing over, it's safe now.

One name left. The one that started all of this.

quests.title: Zalazane
quests.description:
[He is a long time getting to it.]

Zalazane.

There. I've said it to somebody who might end it, and I've wanted to do that for three years.

The Hollow is the last of it. The source. Cave mouth on the south-east island, end of the long bridge off the Landing.

He was a witch doctor of this tribe. He had standing. And when the moment came to lead his own kin he turned them into hexed and drowned things instead, because that was easier than being told no.

That's all he is. I've had three years to find something larger in him and there isn't anything.

Now listen, because this is the fight: he will not raise a weapon until he has tried to turn your own friends against you. That's his opening and it's his whole craft.

Break the hex fast, or don't let it land at all.

That's it. That's really the whole of it.
quests.accept_text: Zalazane's Hollow, south-east island, end of the long bridge off the Landing.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's over. Zalazane is finished and this island belongs to the living again.

I've carried this a long time. I don't fully know how a man puts down a weight that old.

I suspect I'll work it out starting today.

Take what he had. You've more than earned it.

quests.title: A Healer's Debt
quests.description:
Mind the mats. Everything on them is someone.

Zathra. I mend what the camps send down to me - fevers, cuts, curses. The fevers and cuts I've been doing since I was a girl.

The curses are new, and they are all the same curse.

Every single one of them comes in with the same mark on the skin. A sliver of bone pressed into the flesh, with a Darkspear name carved on it - and then the name crossed out.

That's not a hex somebody threw in a fight. That's bookkeeping.

The fetish-carvers make them. They work the camp fires and the deeper dens of the Hollow.

Take the shards off them. Don't touch the names - lay them flat and bring them flat.

And bring enough that I can read them together, because one is a name and a stack of them is a pattern, and I am tired of treating symptoms while the thing making them keeps carving.
quests.accept_text: The carvers work the camp fires and the deeper dens of the Hollow. Don't touch the names.
quests.turn_in_text: ... all one hand. All one rhythm. It's a weaver, mon - someone in da Hollow who stitches dese hexes into da bone. I'll tell you where to look. Take dis for da trouble.

quests.title: The Weaver Behind the Hex
quests.description:
I read them together. I was right and I'd rather not have been.

There is one hand on every shard. One carver, with a den on the west side of Zalazane's Hollow, below the sanctum itself.

Mam'toth. They call him the Hexweaver and he has earned it the hard way.

I have treated forty of his victims. Forty, mon - I have the count because I keep the count, and I keep it because somebody should.

I would like to stop. Not stop healing. Stop healing THIS, over and over, while the loom in that den keeps turning.

His adepts will rally to him the moment you're seen. Go through them.

And when you reach him - interrupt the weave if you can, kill him quickly if you can't. Those are the only two outcomes in that room and one of them is much worse for you.

Bring back whatever's left of the loom. I want to see it broken with my own eyes.
quests.accept_text: West side of the Hollow, in a den below Zalazane's sanctum.
quests.turn_in_text: Forty hexes, unmade in one breath. I felt dem go. Dat's da best medicine I've ever tasted. Take dis - and remember, mon: da healin' was never da hard part. It's da stoppin'.

quests.title: Charts of the Lost Fleet
quests.description:
Jin'zil. I walk this beach at dawn and I've done it thirty years, which makes me either the most patient troll on this island or the least ambitious. Depends who's asking.

Thirty years of rope ends and broken oars and a great deal of nothing.

This morning I found a chart.

Drowned, soaked through, and still legible - washed off one of the dead ships of the Lost Fleet up in the north-east. Somebody took soundings on it. Careful ones.

I want the rest of them.

Because whoever sailed those ships knew where the old reefs lay, and I have come round to thinking the old reefs are where Zalazane draws from. He didn't become what he is out of nothing. Something out there was already old.

The drowned crewmen still carry their charts. They cannot put the job down.

Don't read them in the rain.
quests.accept_text: North-east, past the shallows, at the Lost Fleet. The drowned crewmen still carry them.
quests.turn_in_text: A ring of islands, and a red cross. It's not a treasure map, mon - it's a warnin'. Da man who drew dis was runnin' from somethin'. One of his mates still guards da wreck. I'll tell you where.

quests.title: Barnacle-Beard's Lantern
quests.description:
One more thing out there, and it's not a thing to me.

The first mate of the Lost Fleet never left his post. Old Barnacle-Beard, the beachcombers called him, back when there were enough of us to call him anything.

He walks the shallows by the wrecks with a lantern in one hand and an axe in the other, looking for the captain's orders.

There are no orders. The captain's been down twenty years. He's walking a dark flat looking for a piece of paper that stopped existing before he did, and he will do it until somebody stops him.

The crabs that infest those flats have gone feral on him. Kill them and he'll come looking for the noise - he can't help it, noise is the job.

Bring me the lantern.

And put the old man down properly. He fights like a man who's already dead, mon, and that is not a figure of speech.
quests.accept_text: Wreck Shallows, north-east. The crabs gather where he walks.
quests.turn_in_text: ... He's restin'. I could feel him let go. I'm not a sentimental man, but I'll light dis lantern tonight for him, and for da crew. Take whatever you like off his belt.

quests.title: Salvage Rights
quests.description:
You! Yes, you. Come here, keep your voice down, don't look at the water.

Dritt. Salvager. The plan is not complicated and I'll give you the whole thing because I've got nobody left to keep it from.

Get to the Lost Fleet. Take whatever isn't nailed down. Pay off certain parties. Retire somewhere with weather.

The plan has exactly one flaw and it is the Drowned Causeway - the knee-deep ford running north from this camp to the troll isle.

Murloc spearfishers hold it. Sirens sing from the rocks either side.

So it's a toll road now, friend, and the toll is MY LIFE, which I happen to need for the rest of the plan.

Clear me the spearfishers and the singers both.

I'll make it worth your while. Don't ask where the money's from.
quests.accept_text: The Drowned Causeway, running north from this camp. Spearfishers and the singers both.
quests.turn_in_text: You, friend, are a miracle. A violent, wet miracle. And a business partner, I hope. There's still the seer on the rocks who runs the choir. Come back when you're ready.

quests.title: The Seer on the Rocks
quests.description:
Spearfishers are one thing. Spearfishers I can price.

The thing that sings them into position is a different conversation.

Seer Sshara. She sits on a rock halfway down that causeway and she does not let a sailor past, and she has been doing it longer than I've been on this island.

I had a crew. Seven. Good ones, mostly.

She charmed every single one of them into walking off the end of a pier, in order, while I stood forty feet away shouting, and the last one waved at me.

I would like to be paid back in gold. I will settle for silence.

Now listen, because this is the only advice I have ever given anybody for free: do not listen to her sing. Plug your ears. Wax, cloth, anything. Go deaf for the afternoon.

My crew weren't smart enough and now they're fish.
quests.accept_text: Halfway down the Drowned Causeway, up on the rocks. Plug your ears.
quests.turn_in_text: Silent! You saved my life and about nine thousand gold in lost cargo. I'll find you a bonus, I'm just not quite sure where.

quests.title: The Captain's Strongbox
quests.description:
[Dritt looks genuinely cheerful for the first time.]

Causeway's quiet, so I can finally say the plan out loud instead of implying it.

Captain Morrow went down with his ship. He also went down with his strongbox, which is the operative detail and the reason I came to this archipelago at all.

He's still on his flagship up in the north-east. Dead, armed, and extremely unsociable.

I had a client once, few years back - showed up on this beach talking about a world he'd left behind and a bank that wouldn't follow him here. Finest mood I ever saw on a man. He's the one who told me about Morrow's box.

He was right about the box. He was wrong about the bank, as it turns out.

The flagship's the big one, you won't need directions. Cutlass, temper, probably a grudge.

Bring me that strongbox and I'll buy you a drink. Several.
quests.accept_text: North-east past the troll isle. The flagship's the big one.
quests.turn_in_text: ... it's empty. Is it? No. No, it's not. THERE'S A FALSE BOTTOM! Friend, I'm going to cry in a minute. Take your cut, take it all, take the boat.

quests.title: A Hound's Worth
quests.description:
Last thing and it's not business, it's sleep.

This camp sits a stone's throw from Zalazane's Hollow. I knew that when I pitched it. It was cheap for a reason and I made my choice like an adult.

Every night something in the dark whistles up the shadowfang hounds and they come round my perimeter in the dark, and they don't attack, friend, they just go round.

Houndmaster Gor'tek keeps the kennels in the middle of the Hollow, past the Thrall Pens. The whistle is his.

I can live near hounds. I cannot live near a whistle - because a whistle means somebody decides, and whoever decides can decide differently about me on any night he likes.

Kill the hounds first so the master comes out.

And put him down before he whips the pack into a frenzy, or you'll be buying a great many bandages and I don't extend credit.
quests.accept_text: Middle of the Hollow, past the Thrall Pens. Hounds first, so the master comes out.
quests.turn_in_text: Dead quiet! The whistle's gone and the hounds are asleep. I haven't slept in two weeks. I'm going to sleep for two more. Take dis, with my thanks. And my sympathies for his dogs.

quests.title: Pearls for the Offering
quests.description:
Kesh. Keeper of the spirit-shrine, which is these stones, a few steps from the temple door.

Something's started leaving things on the shrine step that nobody placed there.

I want to be clear about that, mon. I sweep that step at dawn. I know what I put on it and I know what the tide puts on it, and for a month now there has been a third answer.

So the spirits are asking again, and I've not had them ask in my lifetime.

The old offering was always a tide-touched pearl. Grey, damp, impossible to dry - you can leave one in the sun all day and it comes up wet, and nobody has ever explained that to me either.

The only pearls left are inside the temple. The murlocs hoard them in the shallows and the tidal elementals wear them like bad jewellery.

Go in at the temple door, at the end of the Grotto trail. Keep them wet.
quests.accept_text: Inside the temple, at the end of the Grotto trail. Murlocs hoard them; the elementals wear them.
quests.turn_in_text: Five. Perfect. Da tide is already softer. Dese pearls are why da temple's guardians never left. Dey're still lookin' for da last offering. Dere's a drowned warrior down dere who needs rest.

quests.title: The Restless Below
quests.description:
The offering won't take. I've made it twice and twice it sat there, and the reason is underneath us.

The Drowned Crypt, off the west gate of the Grotto's rotunda.

There's a Darkspear warrior down there called Moj'bashi, and he has been walking the same tide-flooded corridor for forty years.

He isn't malicious. I need that said before you go down. I've stood in the water at the mouth of that corridor and watched him turn at the far end and come back, and there's nothing in him that wants anything.

He isn't sane either, and the drowned trolls down there have followed his example, which is what the dead do when somebody keeps walking.

He'll be at the back.

Treat him as a warrior rather than a monster - he'd have wanted that, and I think some part of him still does.

And be quick about it, mon. Forty years is long enough.
quests.accept_text: Off the west gate of the rotunda. He'll be at the back.
quests.turn_in_text: He's at rest. I felt it as he went, like a held breath comin' out. Dat's what da pearls were for. Take dis - da shrine and I are even.

quests.title: A Dare on the Sunken Steps
quests.description:
Hey! HEY. You're the one everybody at the Landing keeps talking about, right?

Muzka. I can hold my breath four minutes. Four. I've had it timed by two people who don't like each other, so it counts.

The Sunken Steps are where I've been proving it. A stair of old black stone that comes up out of the knee-deep water south of the Naga Ruins, between my island and theirs - nobody knows who built it and nobody cares except me.

The steps have guardians. Big slab-shaped things that stand on them and don't move until you're close.

And now the murloc spearfishers have taken an interest, which is unfair, because the murlocs cannot hold their breath at all.

I need a witness. That's the whole job.

From the Grotto isle take the north trail into the water. Reach the middle step, break the sentinels, come back and tell me I'm brave.

My mother has views about this. She may be right. We're doing it anyway.

objectives.label: the Sunken Steps, off the Grotto isle

quests.accept_text: From the Grotto isle, north trail into the water. The steps are right below.
quests.turn_in_text:
You're BRAVE. Say it again, say it where my cousin can hear.

[He stops.]

How many steps were there past the middle one? ... That's what I thought. Nobody ever gets further than that.

quests.title: What Took My Brother's Leg
quests.description:
[The boy isn't joking around this time.]

My brother dove the south-west reef. He came back with half a leg.

I was on the beach. I want to say that because people tell this story like I heard about it later.

The thing that took it is the Razorjaw. Big reef predator - he's had the south-west for ten years and he circles the shallows below the Razorjaw Reef island the moment there's blood in the water.

Everybody on this island knows about him. Everybody goes a different way round, and that's been good enough for everybody, and my brother can't walk.

I don't want revenge. I've thought about it properly and I don't - I'm not sure I'd know what to do with it.

I want it to stop.

South trail till the water, then west across the shallows. His whelps hunt in packs and he comes when they scream.

He hits hard and he gets angrier the longer it runs. Hit and move, mon.
quests.accept_text: South trail to the water, then west across the shallows. The whelps bring him.
